text:
maya: hi! first day — quick env question. my dotfiles wire up asdf + homebrew but i keep getting 'node: command not found' in new shells. i think PATH order is off. using macOS Ventura, zsh. any recommended minimal .zshrc/.zprofile differences?

sam: welcome maya :wave: usually for macos i put brew paths in .zprofile and zsh plugin stuff in .zshrc. asdf needs to be initialized in the login profile so the shims are in PATH early. e.g. in ~/.zprofile:

  export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
  . $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh

then in ~/.zshrc keep aliases, plugins, and compinit.

maya: ah ok — is there a reason to prefer .zprofile over .zshenv/.zshrc? sometimes i followed dotfiles that put everything in .zshrc and it worked in terminal but failed in GUI apps.

nate: short: login vs interactive. macOS Terminal/iTerm launches a login shell by default, GUI apps sometimes don't, and certain tools (editor terminal panes) behave differently. .zprofile is for login shells (good for PATH), .zshrc is for interactive (completions, plugins). .zshenv runs for *every* shell, so avoid heavy stuff there.

maya: that explains it. also hitting EACCES when npm installs global packages: 

  npm WARN checkPermissions Missing write access to /usr/local/lib/node_modules

should i change npm prefix or use asdf node plugin config?

alia: use npmrc to point global installs to home dir or use asdf to manage node versions (recommended). i add this to ~/.npmrc:

  prefix=${HOME}/.npm-global

then add ~/.npm-global/bin to PATH in .zprofile. avoids sudo.

sam: alternatively, if using asdf-nodejs, run `asdf plugin-add nodejs` then `asdf install nodejs 20.14.0` and `asdf global nodejs 20.14.0`. ensure the asdf init runs before your PATH modifications that rely on node. restart shells.

maya: one weirdness — my iTerm tabs show old node version even after `asdf global` changed it. is there a shim cache?

nate: asdf uses shims in ~/.asdf/shims. if you have an older node installed via brew in /opt/homebrew/bin earlier in PATH it will shadow shims. run `which -a node` to see order. you can run `asdf reshim` after installs. also check for leftover /usr/local/bin entries if you migrated from Intel mac.

maya: thanks — ran `which -a node` and saw /opt/homebrew/bin/node first. moved /opt/homebrew/bin after asdf shims in .zprofile and reshim fixed it.

dev-setup-bot: Hi @maya — welcome to Redwood! Quick checklist: 1) Join #dev-setup channel 2) Run the onboarding script: https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard 3) Add your SSH key to the gitlab org. If you need admin for asdf plugin installs, ping @devops.

maya: one last tiny thing — i'm trying to enable zsh-autosuggestions + zsh-syntax-highlighting. do we have a preferred plugin manager? antigen/antibody/zim/oh-my-zsh?

alia: we prefer keeping it simple: no oh-my-zsh heavy frameworks. i use zplug for speed but you can also just clone plugins into ~/.zsh/plugins and source them in .zshrc. example snippet i keep in dotfiles repo:

  if [ -d "$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions" ]; then
    source "$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-autosuggestions/zsh-autosuggestions.zsh"
  fi

we've got a small dotfiles repo: https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles. PRs welcome.

maya: perfect — cloning that now. huge help, thanks everyone :raised_hands:

sam: ping if you hit anything weird. also add your preferred editor + terminal to your onboarding doc so we can add common tweaks to quickstarts.

maya: will do.
